Find Markers Along a Resolution Tree and Build a Dichotomous Key

Source: R/Hierarchical_markers.R
find_hierarchical_markers.Rd

Tracks clusters from low to high resolution and finds, at every point where a cluster splits, the genes that distinguish its sub-clusters. Low resolutions give broad markers of major populations; higher resolutions give finer markers of sub-populations. For every split, a short decision tree (rpart) picks the genes and thresholds that sort cells into the sub-clusters: a dichotomous key.

Usage

find_hierarchical_markers(
  seurat_obj,
  res_cols = NULL,
  pipeline = NULL,
  assay = "RNA",
  padj_max = 0.05,
  min_log2fc = 0.5,
  min_pct = 0.5,
  min_pct_diff = 0.3,
  min_purity = 0.8,
  min_cells = 20,
  specific_auc = 0.8,
  max_candidate_genes = 100,
  max_depth = NULL,
  n_backup = 10,
  cv_folds = 10,
  seed = 42,
  sample_name = "Sample",
  output_dir = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

A Seurat object with normalised data and cluster columns at several resolutions.

res_cols

Character vector of metadata columns holding the clusters, e.g. c("RNA_snn_res.0.2", "RNA_snn_res.0.5", "RNA_snn_res.1"). Ordered by the resolution in their name when it can be read, otherwise used as given. Give this or pipeline.

pipeline

Character. Instead of res_cols: use every <graph>_res.<resolution> column of this method, named as in analyze_and_save_clusters() (e.g. "log.fastmnn" or "RNA_snn").

assay

Character. Assay used for expression. Default is "RNA".

padj_max, min_log2fc, min_pct, min_pct_diff

Numeric marker filters: adjusted p-value below padj_max (default 0.05), avg_log2FC at least min_log2fc (default 0.5), detected in at least min_pct of the child's cells (default 0.5), and detection difference pct.1 - pct.2 at least min_pct_diff (default 0.3).

min_purity

Numeric. Children below this purity are flagged and their markers labelled "unstable" (they are still tested). Default is 0.8.

min_cells

Integer. Children with fewer cells in a split are skipped. Default 20.

specific_auc

Numeric. AUC against all other cells needed for "specific". Default is 0.8.

max_candidate_genes

Integer. Top-ranked markers per child offered to rpart. Default is 100.

max_depth

Integer or NULL. Maximum number of questions on any path of a split's key before pruning. NULL (default) uses the number of children of the split (at most 30).

n_backup

Integer. Backup (surrogate) genes reported per question. Default 10.

cv_folds

Integer. Cross-validation folds for pruning. Default is 10.

seed

Integer. Seed for the cross-validation folds (the global random state is restored afterwards). Default is 42.

sample_name

Character. Used in plot titles and file names. Default "Sample".

output_dir

Character or NULL. If given, the tables (CSV) and plots (JPEG) are saved there. Default is NULL (nothing saved).

verbose

Logical. Print progress messages. Default is TRUE.

Value

A list with:

  • tree: one row per cluster (node): node, layer, resolution, res_col, cluster, parent, n_cells, purity, n_children, low_purity.

  • splits: one row per split: split, layer, children, skipped_children (too few cells), n_cells, n_markers, n_key_genes, cv_accuracy, train_accuracy, status.

  • markers: every gene passing the filters, per split and child: split, child, gene, rank, auc, auc_vs_all, p_val, p_val_adj, avg_log2FC, pct.1, pct.2, pct_diff, mean_child, mean_siblings, also_marks_parent, also_marks_children, pattern.

  • key: the key and backup genes of every split: split, rpart_node, role, gene, threshold, rule (e.g. "GZMK >= 1.2 -> res0.5_3"), high_side (the child predicted for cells at or above the threshold), agreement (backup genes: rpart's adjusted agreement with the key gene), importance, then marker_of and the ranking columns of markers for that gene.

  • confusion: per split, a table of true vs key-predicted child.

  • plots: tree (the resolution tree with key genes at each split) and dotplot (key genes across the clusters of the highest resolution).

  • res_cols and parameters.

Details

1. Tree. Resolutions are ordered from low to high. Each cluster is linked to the cluster of the previous resolution that holds most of its cells (its parent); that share is its purity. Clusterings at different resolutions are not always nested, so a low purity means the cluster takes cells from several parents. The root holds all cells, so its children are the clusters of the lowest resolution. A cluster with a single child (unchanged at the next resolution) is not a split.

2. Markers per split. At each split, every child is compared with its siblings only, using the parent's cells (Seurat::FindMarkers(), Wilcoxon, genes higher in the child). Cells of the parent that moved to a child of another parent are left out. Children with fewer than min_cells cells are skipped. Genes are kept when p_val_adj < padj_max, avg_log2FC >= min_log2fc, pct.1 >= min_pct and pct.1 - pct.2 >= min_pct_diff, then ranked by AUC (the probability that a random child cell expresses the gene more highly than a random sibling cell; 0.5 = no separation, 1 = perfect), with the detection difference as tie-break. Clusters were defined on the same data, so p-values are optimistic: use them as a filter, not as evidence on their own.

3. Patterns. Each marker row gets also_marks_parent (the gene also marks the parent against the parent's siblings), also_marks_children (it also separates the child's own sub-clusters; NA for a child that does not split further) and a pattern:

  • "unstable": the child (or a cluster it passes through unchanged) has a purity below min_purity, so the split is not clean across resolutions;

  • "specific": the child does not split further and the gene also separates it from all other cells (auc_vs_all >= specific_auc);

  • "lineage": the child splits further, but the gene does not separate its sub-clusters (shared by all of them);

  • "split": any other marker of this split.

4. Key. For each split, rpart is given the top max_candidate_genes ranked markers of every child, grown to max_depth questions and pruned by cross-validation (1-SE rule: the smallest tree whose error is within one standard error of the best). The data therefore decide how many genes each split needs. For every question, the chosen gene (role = "key") and up to n_backup surrogate genes that sort the cells almost the same way (role = "backup") are reported with all ranking values.

Expression is read from the data layer of assay; split Seurat v5 layers are joined on a local copy.

See also

analyze_and_save_clusters() to choose resolutions, plot_dot_dendro_multi() to plot the key genes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- find_hierarchical_markers(
  seurat_obj = my_seurat,
  res_cols   = c("RNA_snn_res.0.1", "RNA_snn_res.0.3", "RNA_snn_res.0.8"),
  output_dir = "Hierarchical_markers"
)
res$key                                  # key + backup genes with their ranking values
subset(res$markers, pattern == "lineage")
res$plots$tree

# All resolutions of one integration method
res <- find_hierarchical_markers(my_seurat, pipeline = "log.fastmnn")
} # }
